Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap of needs (from our conversation):
- Primary drivers: reduce per-token costs and improve p50 latency for dropdown search flows.
- Throughput: sustained traffic with periodic peaks during batch jobs.
- Security/compliance: data residency and audit logs matter — procurement will need SOC2 artifacts.
- Migration: currently using another public LLM API plus some on-prem GPU workers for internal models.

Clarifying questions to help me recommend the best deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private):
1) Current traffic: what’s your typical tokens/sec or requests/sec during normal and peak windows?
2) Latency SLO: you mentioned wanting p50 ~150ms — is p99 also a target?
3) Data residency: do you need a VPC/on-prem option for all customer data, or only for a subset of workloads?
4) Timeline: when do you want to cut over/migrate? Any procurement milestones we should know about?

High-level next steps I propose:
- You share the traffic profile (answers to Qs above) + any perf logs you can.
- We schedule a 45-min technical sync with Dylan (our SE) to size Dedicated or Private options and walk through the migration approach.
- We prepare a one-page pilot plan (2-week Dedicated reserved capacity trial) and an SOW draft for procurement.

Attached: deployment-mode-matrix.xlsx — quick comparison and checklist (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

If that plan looks good I’ll book the technical sync — are you available Wed/Thu this week afternoon PT?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — helpful. Answers below: 
- Traffic: avg ~45 requests/sec (text-gen + embeddings), typical token rate ~3k tokens/sec, peaks up to ~18k tokens/sec during batch/market-open spikes.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 ~150ms, we care about p95/p99 for user-facing flows (p99 target ~600–800ms).
- Data residency: regulated workflows (payment & KYC flows) need VPC/isolation; non-sensitive features can run on hosted API. Ideally we want Dedicated capacity with VPC peering for sensitive routes.
- Current infra: mix — primarily using OpenAI’s API for public-facing features, and a small self-hosted GPU cluster (Nvidia T4s) for specific research models.
- Timeline: procurement review in 4–6 weeks; goal to have a pilot in the next 6–8 weeks.

We’re happy to meet Wed afternoon (3/24) PT for the technical sync — cc’d procurement for SOW conversation.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — Deployment recommendation & pilot plan

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick answers — that data is perfect and helps narrow options. Below is a recommended approach and migration modes based on what you shared.

Recommendation (short):
- Pilot: Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering for sensitive routes. This gives the predictable throughput you want and isolates regulated workloads.
- Longer term: Hybrid model — Dedicated for production-sensitive routes + Hosted for lower-risk, high-volume endpoints to reduce cost. If strict on-premures are required we can scope Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) as a follow-on.

Rationale and notes: 
- Dedicated: matches your peak token needs and lets us size burst capacity; supports audit logs/KMS integration for compliance.
- Hosted: lower operational cost and fastest time-to-value for non-sensitive features.
- Private: recommended only if procurement/legal insists on no public-cloud control plane or air-gapped requirements — higher ops overhead.

Migration modes (practical):
1) Lift-and-shift from other LLM API: map prompts + tokenization differences, validate responses against baseline, and run A/B traffic split during the pilot.
2) Self-hosted clusters: if you want to move local model weights, we assist with model compatibility checks and runtime tuning (quantization, kernel selection).
3) Hybrid routing: smart routing rules (latency vs cost) so sensitive requests route to Dedicated/VPC and others go to Hosted.

Immediate next steps I’ll take:
- Draft a 2-week Dedicated pilot SOW and pricing (attached as pilot-sow-draft.pdf).
- Book a 45-min technical sizing session with Dylan to confirm instance types and burst settings (I propose Wed 3/24 2:00pm PT).
- Share SOC2 and compliance artifacts for procurement.

Can you confirm: 1) Wed 3/24 2pm PT works for the technical sync? 2) Who from your infra team should join so we can review cluster configs and logs?

Thanks — I’ll also add the HubSpot deal and DocuSign links for procurement in a separate note.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198
